key_insight: Nonlinearity-subtracted DMD (NSDMD) uses nonlinear-term snapshots to recover a low-rank, mean-flow-linearized operator from data, enabling resolvent-style analysis without specialized linear-solver infrastructure.
engineering_relevance: This makes linear modal analysis of turbulent flows practical as a post-processing step on DNS/LES data, even for complex geometries such as a full aircraft model.
method: Compute DMD while subtracting the explicit contribution of nonlinear forcing in the perturbation equations.
Use the resulting operator as a data-driven approximation of mean-flow-linearized dynamics.
Apply the framework to data-driven resolvent analysis across simple and complex turbulent flows.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports demonstrations on DNS and LES datasets, progressing from a minimal channel flow to a full aircraft model.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and availability of nonlinear-term snapshots, and the learned operator is still an approximation of the underlying linearized physics.
paper_title: Data-driven linear analysis of turbulent flows
